newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Six Israeli police charged with assaulting Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Six Israeli police charged with assaulting Arabs.

text.p: Israel on Sunday charged six paramilitary policemen with beating Arabs, issuing two separate indictments that graphically depicted alleged brutality towards Palestinians caught in the Jewish state without permits.

Border policemen Tsahi Shamaya, 19, and David Ben Abu, 20, were charged with beating six Palestinians. An amateur Palestinian cameraman filmed last month's assault and the videotape was broadcast worldwide last week.
"The accused dealt the detainees blows, punches, slaps and kicks to all parts of their bodies," a charge sheet, released by the courts, said of Shamaya and Ben Abu.
"(They) brutalised the detainees and degraded them by compelling three of them to do push-ups. One sat on the head of a detainee and rode him," it said.
One of the policemen punched a passerby in the face after he tried to persuade the officers to cease the beatings.
In a second case in the Jerusalem court, four border policemen were alleged to have taken Fadi Muhammad Shawwar to a wooded area and beaten him unconscious after detaining him in the city last June.
The charge sheet said the policemen Oren Eldi, Benny Deri, Assaf Shahar and Meir Albaz kicked and punched Shawwar while driving him to the wood.
"Upon arriving in the wood...Defendent One grabbed the plaintiff by the shirt and forced him off the jeep. Defendent Two hit the plaintiff with his nightstick and kicked him." the charge sheet said.

"Defendent Three or Four ordered the plaintiff to spread his legs then kicked him in the groin. The plaintiff fell to the ground and Defendents Two, Three and Four continued to beat him...Defendent One took his stick and hit the plaintiff in the head." it said.
The charge sheet said the four left the bruised and scarred Shawwar unconscious in the wood.
Palestinians have often complained of abuse by paramilitary border policemen stationed throughout the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the incident caught on video and said it was rare. Israeli human rights groups said that incident was unique only in that it was captured on video.
All six policemen were charged with aggravated assault and abuse of authority. They have yet to enter pleas.
